pointers.sentence: `django/utils/dateparse.py` reads a date, a time, a datetime or a duration from text, with `parse_date`, `parse_time`, `parse_datetime` and `parse_duration`; `django/utils/duration.py` writes a duration back as text; and `django/utils/ipv6.py` checks an IPv6 address and gives it one spelling, with `clean_ipv6_address`.

`django/utils/dateparse.py` reads a date, a time, a datetime or a duration from text, with `parse_date`, `parse_time`, `parse_datetime` and `parse_duration`; `django/utils/duration.py` writes a duration back as text; and `django/utils/ipv6.py` checks an IPv6 address and gives it one spelling, with `clean_ipv6_address`.

A model's date, time or datetime field turns `None` into its `"invalid"` error and `ValueError` into `"invalid_date"`, `"invalid_time"` or `"invalid_datetime"`, so that its message says whether the format or the value was wrong (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:DateField.to_python`).

`normalize_json` makes a task's arguments and return value the types of JSON ([Background tasks: `Task`, `TaskResult` and the task backends](../services/tasks.md)) (`django/utils/json.py:normalize_json`).

`parse_date`, `parse_time` and `parse_datetime` each try their type's own fromisoformat first, `datetime.datetime.fromisoformat` for a datetime, and the module's pattern only when that raises `ValueError`, passing the pattern's groups as integers to the type's constructor (`django/utils/dateparse.py:parse_datetime`).

On the pattern's path `"Z"` becomes `datetime.UTC`, and another offset is counted in minutes and given to `get_fixed_timezone`, which returns a `datetime.timezone` named after it (`django/utils/timezone.py:get_fixed_timezone`).
The pattern has no place for an offset, so text the standard library refuses gives `None` if it carries one, the case the docstring describes (`django/utils/dateparse.py:parse_time`).

The parsers' main callers are SQLite's converters, which the driver runs on each date, time and datetime column it fetches ([Values in and out: adapters, converters and time zones](../backends/values.md)) (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:decoder`); a model field's `to_python`, given a string ([The field classes](../models/field-types.md)); and the form field `DateTimeField`, before its input formats ([The built-in form fields](../forms/field-types.md)) (`django/forms/fields.py:DateTimeField.to_python`).

`parse_duration` tries three patterns in turn and uses the first that matches (`django/utils/dateparse.py:parse_duration`).

Text in no form gives `None`; a duration too long for a `datetime.timedelta` raises `OverflowError`, which the form field `DurationField` reports as `"overflow"` (`django/forms/fields.py:DurationField.to_python`) and the model field lets through.
`parse_duration` reads weeks in ISO 8601's form, `"P1W"` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
`django/utils/duration.py` writes two of the forms.

`duration_string` writes Django's own, with days and microseconds only where there are some, and a negative duration as Python holds it, negative days and a positive time (`django/utils/duration.py:duration_string`); a model's `DurationField.value_to_string` gives it to a serializer (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:DurationField.value_to_string`).

`duration_string` writes Django's own, with days and microseconds only where there are some, and a negative duration as Python holds it, negative days and a positive time (`django/utils/duration.py:duration_string`); a model's `DurationField.value_to_string` gives it to a serializer (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:DurationField.value_to_string`).

`duration_iso_string` writes ISO 8601, for `DjangoJSONEncoder.default` (`django/core/serializers/json.py:DjangoJSONEncoder.default`) and for Oracle's schema editor, which quotes a duration with it (`django/db/backends/oracle/schema.py:DatabaseSchemaEditor.quote_value`).

`duration_iso_string` writes ISO 8601, for `DjangoJSONEncoder.default` (`django/core/serializers/json.py:DjangoJSONEncoder.default`) and for Oracle's schema editor, which quotes a duration with it (`django/db/backends/oracle/schema.py:DatabaseSchemaEditor.quote_value`).

`duration_microseconds` makes the integer that `BaseDatabaseOperations.adapt_durationfield_value` hands the driver, which PostgreSQL's and Oracle's override to pass the `datetime.timedelta` on (`django/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseDatabaseOperations.adapt_durationfield_value`).
An IPv6 address can be spelt many ways, and `clean_ipv6_address` gives it the one `ipaddress.IPv6Address` writes, compressed and in lower case (`django/utils/ipv6.py:clean_ipv6_address`).

It refuses text longer than its max_length argument, by default `MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH`, 39, eight full groups, a bound added against a denial of service, CVE-2024-56374 (`docs/releases/5.1.5.txt`); parses the text; and makes the address an integer and an address again, which drops a scope such as `"%eth0"` (`django/utils/ipv6.py:_ipv6_address_from_str`).

It refuses text longer than its max_length argument, by default `MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH`, 39, eight full groups, a bound added against a denial of service, CVE-2024-56374 (`docs/releases/5.1.5.txt`); parses the text; and makes the address an integer and an address again, which drops a scope such as `"%eth0"` (`django/utils/ipv6.py:_ipv6_address_from_str`).

`is_valid_ipv6_address` asks the same without raising: an `ipaddress.IPv6Address` is valid at once, and anything else is parsed under the default limit, `TypeError` and `ValueError` both meaning `False`; `validate_ipv6_address` is built on it (`django/core/validators.py:validate_ipv6_address`).

The model's and the form's `GenericIPAddressField.to_python` strip a value and call `clean_ipv6_address` if it has a colon, the form's with its own `max_length` ([The field classes](../models/field-types.md), [The built-in form fields](../forms/field-types.md)) (`django/forms/fields.py:GenericIPAddressField.to_python`).
